mechanics.name: Blood Rush
mechanics.currentEffect: After being unhooked by any means, the perk activates for 40/50/60 seconds. While active, use the Active Ability button to instantly recover from an existing Exhausted status. It does not cause Exhausted. A Conspicuous Action ends it early; using it deactivates it, and it is disabled for the rest of the Trial once the Exit Gates are powered.
activation: Use the Active Ability while Exhausted during the activation window.
Ends/deactivates when: A Conspicuous Action ends it early.
Ends/deactivates when: It deactivates after use and is disabled once Exit Gates are powered.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.3.0): Reworked into the current post-unhook Exhausted-removal effect.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: After an unhook, use a limited window to remove Exhausted once without receiving Exhausted again.
mechanics.oncePerTrialOrOtherLimits: Once used, deactivates; disabled for remainder of Trial when Exit Gates are powered.
specialInteractions: Blood Rush itself does not cause Exhausted.

editorial.summary: After an unhook, gain a limited window where you can instantly clear an existing Exhausted status once, potentially bringing a powerful Exhaustion perk back online.
useCases: Reset Sprint Burst, Lithe, Dead Hard, or another Exhaustion perk during the dangerous post-unhook window.
Turn an expected tunnel chase into a second Exhaustion-perk activation the Killer may not be prepared for.
Use the threat of another chase burst to reach a safer area after rescue.
counters: Only activates after an unhook and expires after the short activation window.
Conspicuous Actions end the opportunity early.
It is disabled once the Exit Gates are powered.
pros: Can effectively create a second use of an elite chase perk.
No health-state sacrifice in its modern form.
cons: Completely inactive before your first unhook.
analysis: Blood Rush leads this band because resetting Exhaustion is one of the more powerful effects a Survivor perk can offer. Exhaustion perks are deliberately limited by downtime, so removing that downtime during the most dangerous post-unhook portion of the match can radically change a tunnel chase.

The strongest use is not random activation. It is planning around a specific second chase tool. A Survivor who used Sprint Burst before going down, or who needs Dead Hard available again after rescue, can create a second layer of chase protection that the Killer may not expect.

The perk also improved significantly from its older, harsher form. It no longer requires sacrificing a health state to clear Exhaustion, which makes the current version much more practical as anti-tunnel utility rather than a desperation gimmick.

It remains B because the activation is narrow and temporary. You must be unhooked, already Exhausted, and able to use the reset before a Conspicuous Action or the timer ends. When those pieces line up, Blood Rush can perform above this rank.
editorial.verdict: A high-ceiling post-unhook Exhaustion reset. Blood Rush is narrow, but when paired with an elite Exhaustion perk it can make a tunnel chase unexpectedly expensive.
